RWA.note: A digital signature is only planned at age 16; no authentication service is stated.
No link between civil register and ID system is stated.
No count or share of people enrolled is given.

facts.fact: Rwandan authorities say children will now be integrated into the national digital ID system from birth, with a photo added at four, fingerprints and iris at five, and a digital signature update at sixteen.

RWA.note: Document does not say who operates, maintains or owns the system.
No public register keyed on the ID number is named.

facts.fact: The document says Rwanda is progressively rolling out a new biometric ID card, with photo, fingerprint and iris data collected into a central database, with transition to June 2027 after which old cards are deactivated.

Immigration, with the refugee ministry and UNHCR, is running a registration campaign in all refugee camps and urban centres to issue refugees the new biometric ID cards; a large share at Mahama (over 70,000 refugees) is already registered.
A Kigali urban refugee says that with the earlier refugee ID cards they could open bank accounts and buy SIM cards.
